![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14067289/assets/3387790df770ac8645058c6f460b1f1285629d18d765668e362a8070ae4035ed.png)

Find the arc length of the polar curve $r=2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \pi $ (shown in blue in the diagram above).

*Hint: You may wish to use the following identity: $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\sqrt{\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}}.$*
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(2+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4+8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8+8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{8}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we recall the identity for $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2}):$

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\sqrt{\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}}
$$

Therefore, using $x=\theta $ in the previous identity, the integral can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =2\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{2{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={4\cdot 2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2}))|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =8(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The arc length L of a polar curve r=r(θ) is given by

L=∫θ1θ2r2+(drdθ)2dθ.

Since r=2+2cos⁡θ, we have

drdθ=−2sin⁡θ.

Therefore, the arc length is

L=∫θ1θ2r2+(drdθ)2dθ=∫0π(2+2cos⁡θ)2+(−2sin⁡θ)2dθ=∫0π4+8cos⁡θ+4cos2⁡θ+4sin2⁡θdθ=∫0π8+8cos⁡θdθ=8∫0π1+cos⁡θdθ Now, we recall the identity for cos⁡(x2): cos⁡(x2)=1+cos⁡x2

Therefore, using x=θ in the previous identity, the integral can be written as follows: L=22∫0π2cos2⁡(θ2)dθ=22⋅2⋅∫0πcos⁡(θ2)dθ=4⋅2(sin⁡(θ2))|0π=8(sin⁡(π2)−sin⁡(0))=8.
